items.synopsis: Data still seems to be streaming somewhere when the DialOut (Established) connection on the port is already closed
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, the existing gRPC-DialOut connection does not disconnect completely on the DUT, causing any other DialOut connections to fail.

items.synopsis: ACX7024 see's a "\" character in show chassis hardware output
items.description: Whenever the USB device brand Rally2 is connected to USB port A, a stale /dev/sda entry is being created, which results in junk characters being printed in the show chassis hardware output. To address this issue a fix has been added to verify whether the opened device is a valid block device. If it's not, the code now skips to the next iteration without processing it. Added logic to sanitize the device string by replacing junk characters with spaces. Introduced additional checks to validate block count and size, preventing further processing of dummy or invalid devices.

items.synopsis: The rpd process crashes after BGP configuration commits involving group-split-size and RIB-sharding
items.description: On Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, configuring "group-split-size" with BGP RIB-sharding(Border Gateway Protocol Routing Information Base Sharding) can lead to a crash in the routing protocol daemon (rpd) when a route update for a non-negotiated NLRI(Network Layer Reachability Information) is received in the update thread. This occurs if the NLRI is targeted at other BGP peers within the group that have negotiated it.

items.synopsis: BGP Prefix-SID Label collision causing RPD crash
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, In Segment Routing the RPD ( Routing Protocol Daemon ) crash was observed due to different prefixes were trying to use same label, when Bgp prefix SID ( Segment Identifier ) feature was configured and labels were derived using the SID index.

items.category: PFE L2 forwarding features on BT based platforms
items.synopsis: On PTX EVO platforms in EVPN-VXLAN scenario traffic will not egress out of the irb next-hop when the bridge-domain doesn't have VXLAN VNI configured
items.description: On all PTX Evolved platforms that support EVPN-VXLAN (Ethernet VPN-Virtual Extensible LAN), when the PTX router acts as a MAC-VRF (Media Access Control - Virtual Routing and Forwarding) EVPN gateway, it will fail to forward traffic routed through the 'irb' interface due to packets being discarded at PFE (packet forwarding Engine), causing packet loss.

items.synopsis: BFD single hop session flaps seen after a link down event on Junos evolved ACX platform
items.description: On all Junos Evolved ACX platform with single-hop BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) configured, continuous flapping of the BFD session is seen. When a BFD session drops and reconnects it can cause traffic to be rerouted repeatedly which can lead to intermittent downtime.

items.synopsis: EXP rewrite rules stop working on AE interfaces after system reboot
items.description: When a system reboot is performed, the rewrite profile and the operational processes bound to it are not correctly programmed in hardware. As a result, the EXP rewrite rule setup on Aggregated Ethernet interfaces no longer functions affecting traffic classification and prioritization.

items.synopsis: ACX7k IFL configured with output-traffic-control-profile continues to use IFD VOQ until ethernet-switching table is cleared.
items.description: When modifying the output-traffic-control-profile of a logical interface associated with and IRB with active traffic flows, the flows will continue to use the previously configured egress queues until the mac-address is cleared from the ethernet-switching MAC table.

items.synopsis: Storm Control stops working on all LAG members after deactivating one or more interfaces on Junos OS Evolved ACX7K platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX7K platforms, when storm control is configured on a LAG (Link Aggregation Group) interface and one or more LAG member interfaces are deactivated, storm control stops working on all remaining active members. This results in an immediate increase in BUM (Broadcast, Unknown Unicast, and Multicast) traffic on the egress interface.

items.synopsis: VSTP convergence failure on Junos OS Evolved ACX7K when IRB shares bridge domain with VSTP enabled IFL
items.description: On all Junos Evolved ACX7K platforms, when a VLAN Spanning Tree Protocol (VSTP) enabled Layer 2 logical interface (IFL) shares a bridge domain with an Integrated Routing and Bridging (IRB) interface, VSTP fails to converge due to Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) packets are misrouted to the IRB interface, preventing them from reaching the VSTP process. This causes potential traffic loops due to lack of VSTP convergence.

items.synopsis: Framing error observed on AE interface after performing RE switchover on Junos OS Evolved ACX7509 platform
items.description: Continuous increase in framing errors observed on AE interface after doing RE switchover on Junos OS Evolved ACX7509 platform.

items.synopsis: Traffic loss observed after routing engine reboot or core interface flap on ACX7K platforms
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved ACX7K Platforms, Layer 3 traffic loss can occur after an RE (Routing Engine) reboot or core interface flap due to a race condition between ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) and VPLS (Virtual Private LAN Service) programming.

items.category: System Management daemon and related issues
items.synopsis: On Junos OS Evolved based platforms "Sysman.re" crash file might be observed in particular conditions
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved based platforms, when the RE (Routing Engine) node experiences switchover, offline/online transitions, or rebooting, a 'Sysman.re' crash file might appear in rare cases and could cause traffic impact.

items.synopsis: Unexpected commit failure will be observed when deactivating of unit or changing any configuration and performing a commit operation
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, if input-vlan-map and output-vlan-map are configured, an unexpected commit failure may occur when deactivating a unit (e.g., unit ) or making any configuration changes followed by a commit operation. This issue results in commit failure errors and prevents further configuration changes.

items.synopsis: AE interfaces flap during GRES following an RE reboot on all Junos Evolved platforms
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, Aggregate Ethernet (AE) interfaces with LACP configured will experience a flap due to a timing issue when Graceful Routing Engine Switchover (GRES) is performed after a Routing Engine (RE) reboot, resulting in traffic loss during the flap.

items.synopsis: Adding a new key to authentication-key-chain causes kernel crash
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, when setting/changing the tolerance value of key-chain to max value of 4294967295 and committing and then adding a new key to a key-chain and performing a commit action will result in kernel crash. Device self-recovers after the crash. "show system core-dumps" can be used to check the core. Core name starts with vmcore

items.synopsis: The snmpwalk for OID ifJnxInputErrors is not working on Junos Evolved platforms
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, the snmpwalk for OID ifJnxInputErrors (1.3.6.1.4.1.2636.3.3.1.1.36) is not working. This issue has no impact on traffic.

items.category: Category for software tracing Infra issues
items.synopsis: Configuration under "set system trace application " gets lost during rollback with certain sequence of steps
items.description: On Junos-EVO platforms, configuration under to "set system trace application " gets lost during rollback with sequence of steps. Steps: 1. Seen if commit delta-export configured ("set system commit delta-export"). 2. Configure trace under "set system trace application " and commit. 3. Do rollback 1 but without committing again do rollback, commit. Configuration changes under trace will be lost on commit

items.synopsis: The rpd EVPN module sends a redundant license message to the license infrastructure
items.description: On Junos platforms, when loading the baseline configuration or during BGP flaps or Routing Instance deactivation, and a large number of Group-Based Policy (GBP) tagged routes are removed, a redundant GBP license update message is sent to the license infrastructure for every route deletion. This issue has no impact on traffic.

items.category: Common PR category for all EVO AFT based L2 features related issues on Express platforms
items.synopsis: In scale EVPN scenario with IRB, host traffic via IRB will be impacted ICMP, OSPF, BGP and L3 protocols on Junos Evolved OS PTX series platform
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX series platforms, in a scale EVPN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network) scenario with IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging), the traffic via IRB will be impacted ICMP, OSPF, BGP and L3 protocols.

items.synopsis: SCU/DCU match is not working when configured along with the forwarding-class
items.description: On PTX Junos OS Evolved platforms, the SCU/DCU (Source class usage/ Destination class usage) match is not working when it is configured along with the forwarding-class.

items.synopsis: Incorrect timer error observed in PTP after chassis-control restart
items.description: On Junos Evolved ACX7332 and ACX7348 platforms configured with PTP Telecom profile-type G.8275.1 in T-GM (Timing-Grand Master) mode, incorrect timer error is observer for a short duration upon issuing "restart chassis-control" CLI command. There is no traffic impact due to this issue.

items.synopsis: Configuring the port to 400G without inserting an optical transceiver causes the interface to disappear
items.description: When interface speed is configured as 400G and other relevant ports are marked as unused so that port can support 400G, the interface disappears and is not visible in the show interface terse output. Issue is observed on FPC: ACX7300-2CD4C without a 400G optics present on the device

items.synopsis: PCIe fatal error resulting in an unexpected device reboot and evo-pfemand crash on Junos OS Evolved ACX7322 platform
items.description: On the Junos OS Evolved ACX7332 platform, an unexpected device reboot and evo-pfemand (Evolved Packet Forwarding Engine management process) process crash will be observed, due to PCIe (Peripheral Component Interconnect Express) fatal error "DPC: ERR_FATAL PCI error". This error results in a PCIe link-down event, causing a loss of signal to the external TCAM (Ternary Content Addressable Memory). When the TCAM becomes unavailable, any software attempt to access the TCAM can trigger a PCIe link failure, leading to a complete traffic impact. These events are logged in the system's journal logs.

items.synopsis: Auto-negotiation mismatches leading to connectivity issues on Junos OS Evolved ACX7509, ACX7332, and ACX7348 platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX7509, ACX7332, and ACX7348 platforms having auto-negotiation is configured on a 1G interface, connectivity issues will occur under certain conditions: system reboots or FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator) restarts or changes in auto-negotiation settings on the peer side. In these scenarios, ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) resolution will fail due to a mismatch in the auto-negotiation state between the local and peer interfaces. The local interface will incorrectly appear as UP, while the peer interface shows as DOWN, leading to link-level inconsistencies and loss of connectivity.

items.synopsis: The other port in a port group goes down after an RE switchover if one of the port in the port group is already down on an ACX7509
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX7509 platforms, when one port in a channelized group (like ports 0 in a port group consisting of port 0 and port 1) is already in 'down' state in a ACX7509-FPC-16C with 16x100G-QSFP, performing a Routing Engine (RE) switchover or restarting the picd process can cause the other port in the port group to go down. This will lead to disruption of services running on the port.

items.synopsis: ACX7509 and QFX5700 may report SSD DMA error on secondary disk.
items.description: ACX7509 and QFX5700 may report below SSD DMA error on secondary disk. In most cases there is no operational impact observed. New firmware being packaged into software via this PR fix will resolve this issue.

items.category: Libjtask for RPD tasks, scheduler, timers, memory, and slip
items.synopsis: The process rpd is cored while adding or removing dynamic-tunnels
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, the indexing of next hop while adding or deleting dynamic tunnels causes the rpd process to core and restart. This is a timing issue.

items.synopsis: IFL configured on the LAG interface goes down when the VLAN operation is changed
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when EVPN is configured with the 'df-election-granularity per-esi' feature, any change in VLAN operation causes the IFL (logical interface) configured on the LAG (Link Aggregation Group) interface to go down, impacting all services associated with that interface.

items.synopsis: MVPN Source PE might incorrectly send mcast traffic on SPT while actual receiver is still on RPTree
items.description: In currently flow when a provider tunnel is being deleted, it is assumed the cmcast routes associated to the ptnl would've have been updated before. This is fine for inclusive tunnels, however for selective tunnels especially wild card scenarios the cmcast routes may not be updated. So in cases where the ptnl is deleted like configuration based removal or underlying tunnel going down, there is chance that the forwarding routes are still not deleted. The cmcasts are deleted later in the flow but when they are deleted the corresponding forwarding routes are still not deleted since there is no corresponding ptnl for the cmcast. This will create issues if forwarding is supposed to happen via different forwarding entry like a , G entry but since the more specific S, G stale entry exists, traffic will hit the later and lead to unexpected behavior like traffic black-holing if S, G is Pruned entry.

items.synopsis: High memory and CPU usage due to unintended phone-home client activation
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, high memory and CPU usage may occur if the phone-home client (PHC) is unintentionally triggered, such as when the device boots with factory default settings or when phone-home is manually configured. This can lead to system slowness, crashes, and eventual device reboots.

items.synopsis: QFX5700: SFP+-10G-ACU1M : DAC Cable port down on after performing jack out and jack in.
items.description: QFX5700: SFP+-10G-ACU1M : DAC Cable port down on after performing jack out and jack in. This issue will not be seen if the recommended procedure for cable jack-out and jack-in is followed: 1. Disable the interface from EVO configuration 2. Jack-out the cable 3. Jack-in the cable (or another cable) 4. Re-enable the interface from the EVO configuration If the recommended procedure is not followed, and a jack-out/jack-in is performed, this issue will be hit. To come out of this situation, the workaround is to disable and re-enable the affected interface from EVO configuration.

items.category: Category for QFX5K EVO Platform Software PRs related to Chas
items.synopsis: QFX5230-64CD, QFX5240-64OD, QFX5240-64QD: USB stick will continue to show up under "show chassis hardware detail" even after unplugging from the device
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved QFX platforms QFX5230-64CD, QFX5240-64OD and QFX5240-64QD, inserting and removing the USB flash device & running "show hardware chassis details" command will lead to show the details of USB even. after removing it from device

items.category: RPD Next-hop issues including indirect, CNH, and MCNH
items.synopsis: The rpd crash would be observed when two separate next-hops in rpd map to the same next-hop-index in the kernel
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, when a route is getting installed to the forwarding table, associated next-hops also get installed in the forwarding table. As part of this installation process, the Junos kernel allocates the next-hop-index for the next-hop. The rpd sets this next-hop-index in its database when two separate next-hops for instance NH1 and NH2 in the rpd map to the same next-hop NH in the kernel. In such case, NH1 and NH2 next-hops in rpd will have the same next-hop-index leading to the rpd crash.

items.synopsis: Record Route Object displayed in show mpls lsp output is trucated if number of hops is sixteen or more
items.description: If the number of RSVP LSP hops is sixteen or higher, the RRO displayed in show mpls lsp extensive output may get truncated

items.synopsis: More bandwidth may be admitted onto a TE link when Label Switched Paths (LSPs) undergoing make-before-break re-route over the same link carrying the bypass LSP during local repair
items.description: If Label Switched Paths (LSPs) undergo local repair and subsequently undergo global repair in make-before-break fashion such that the LSPs are re-routed over the same TE link that carries the bypass LSP that protect the LSPs during local repair, then more re-routed LSPs may be admitted on the TE link carrying the bypass LSP than that should be admitted. This may result in some re-routed LSPs remaining on the TE link causing additional traffic sent on the TE link than the capacity of the TE link.

items.synopsis: Configured TFTP server connection and rate limits are not applied
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms configured as Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) server , "connection-limit" or "rate-limit" values are not updated as per configured values.

items.synopsis: Optic Firmware Upgrade script update - to support modules without auto-paging
items.description: This change brings in a software to support firmware upgrade for an optic module with or without auto-paging capability - irrespective of any vendor.

items.category: System Management daemon and related issues
items.synopsis: The l2cpd-agent crashes due to its state cleaned up during shutdown
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, due to a timing issue, it is observed that the l2cpd agent crashes when the app's state is being cleaned by external garbage collection as app is about to shutdown. But there is no traffic impact due to this issue.

items.category: System Management daemon and related issues
items.synopsis: System stops responding to "show system applications app ndp detail" command or prevents applications from start/stop/restart
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, a failure in internal process communication will cause the system to stop responding to the "show system applications app ndp detail" CLI command or prevent applications from start/stop/restart. This issue occurs when systemd becomes unresponsive to requests initiated by sysman. There is no impact to traffic forwarding.

items.synopsis: Interfaces with the same outer VLAN ID but different inner vlans or inner-lists/ranges are reporting a commit error
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, When an interface configured with the same outer VLAN ID but with different inner vlans or inner-lists/ranges, reports a commit error.

items.synopsis: In ACX7000 Routers Platform dependency errors caused by an incomplete SXE interface deletion may prevent the creation of L2 IFLs.
items.description: In ACX7000 Routers Platform dependency errors caused by an incomplete SXE interface deletion may prevent the creation of L2 IFLs.

items.synopsis: EVO: RPC and CLI validation failed for cli "show ethernet-switching table"
items.description: RPC and CLI validation failed for cli "show ethernet-switching table"

items.category: Libjtask for RPD tasks, scheduler, timers, memory, and slip
items.synopsis: Memory leak when deactivating/reactivating routing instances with vrf-table-label
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, a memory leak occurs when a routing instance configured with "vrf-table-label" is deactivated and then reactivated, followed by a Routing Engine (RE) switchover on dual RE systems. This issue causes a slow memory leak in the system.

items.synopsis: Multicast Traffic loss (20s - 30s) is seen during the reconvergence after link flap
items.description: On Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, When device is configured with MoFRR(Multicast-Only Fast Reroute) and PIM(Protocol Independent Multicast) and also when the upstream links to the source of the multicast traffic flow is made down and then up . Traffic loss is seen for around 20 to 30 seconds until the link comes up.

items.category: Issues related to krt-async routing infrastructure
items.synopsis: VPLS session stays down after interface flaps
items.description: An LSI IFL remains in RPD even after being deleted by the interface manager daemon. It is visible in show interface routing but not in show interfaces, indicating that RPD still holds the IFL despite its removal elsewhere. rpd-agent does not send a delete message to RPD due to a reference count issue. Another daemon?likely l2ald?still holds a reference to the IFL. rpd-agent only sends the delete once all references are cleared, which doesn't happen in this case. The fix is to send a "delete pending" message from rpd-agent to RPD. RPD will treat this as a delete and remove the IFL, ensuring consistency across the system.

items.category: UI Infrastructure - mgd, DAX API, DDL/ODL
items.synopsis: XML validation failure may be seen with the "show host | display xml validate" command
items.description: The XML output of "show host| display xml validate" command results in the "WARNING: Received the tag , the output may not have been properly xmlized." error.

items.synopsis: JUNOS: Netconf: Edit-config with operation attribute create for existing hierarchy is not working as per RFC 6241
items.description: JUNOS: Netconf: Edit-config with operation attribute create for existing hierarchy is not working as per RFC 6241

items.synopsis: Host 0 Active Disk Usage Exceeded is not getting cleared even if the usage is less
items.description: On Junos Evolved ACX7024 and ACX7024X, the "Active Disk Usage Exceeded" alarm is raised and not cleared even if the usage is less than 50%. This issue has no impact on traffic.
